items.prompt: A model gives S(0,3) = 0.92 for a name that has survived to valuation time 0. Which interpretation is correct?

options.label: The modeled probability of no default through year 3 is 92%
The modeled probability of default by year 3 is 92%
The three-year discount factor is necessarily 0.92

items.explanation: S(0,3) is the model's probability, conditional on survival at valuation time, that no default occurs through year 3.

items.prompt: Under the same model and valuation time, name A has five-year survival probability 0.84 and name B has five-year survival probability 0.93. Which conclusion is supported?

options.label: Name A has the larger modeled probability of default by year 5
Name B has the larger modeled probability of default by year 5
The two names have the same modeled probability of default by year 5

items.explanation: Lower survival to the same horizon implies higher cumulative default probability to that horizon: 1 - 0.84 exceeds 1 - 0.93.

items.prompt: A model gives two-year survival probability S(0,2) = 0.93. Enter the cumulative probability of default by year 2 as a decimal.
Viewed from valuation time 0, survival probabilities are S(0,1) = 0.97 and S(0,2) = 0.91. Enter the unconditional probability of default during the interval from year 1 to year 2 as a decimal.
items.explanation: The interval default probability is S(0,1) - S(0,2) = 0.97 - 0.91 = 0.06.

items.prompt: In the lesson model, what does a hazard rate at time t describe?

options.label: Instantaneous default intensity conditional on survival to time t
Cumulative default probability from time 0 through time t
The interest rate used to discount every cash flow

items.explanation: Hazard is an instantaneous conditional intensity with inverse-time units, not a cumulative probability or discount rate.

items.prompt: Two names have survived to the same instant. Name A's current hazard rate is 2% per year and name B's is 5% per year. Over the next very short interval, which statement matches the hazard interpretation?

options.label: Name B has the higher modeled conditional default likelihood
Name A has the higher modeled conditional default likelihood
The rates alone prove both names have already defaulted

items.explanation: Conditional on both names having survived to the instant, the higher current hazard corresponds to greater modeled default likelihood over a sufficiently short next interval.

items.prompt: Under the constant-hazard exponential model, calculate the dimensionless three-year survival probability for an annual hazard rate of 2% (0.02 per year).
Under the constant-hazard exponential model, calculate the dimensionless survival probability over 18 months for an annual hazard rate of 3.2% (0.032 per year).
items.explanation: Eighteen months is 1.5 years, so survival is exp(-0.032 × 1.5) = exp(-0.048) = 0.9531337871.
